pull.title: Detect transaction problems early during deserialization
pull.body:
This is split off from #36521 (and not included in #36895), as it's effectively an independent improvement.

This introduces a number of additional checks that are applied during transaction deserialization, which reduce various worst case deserialization time scenarios:
* Reject transactions with more txins or more txouts than can possibly fit in a block (applied always)
* Reject transactions with 0 txins or 0 txouts (applied in P2P code only; there are RPCs like `fundrawtransaction` that explicitly support transactions with 0 inputs)
* Count weight accurately during transaction or block deserialization, and bail out as soon as it exceeds 4M (applied in P2P code).

This is a mild behavior change, as detecting these problems early causes them to be treated as deserialization errors, which in P2P logic cause messages to be ignored instead of peer disconnection.

events.message:
primitives: reject txs with more inputs or outputs than fit in a block

When deserializing a transaction, read the input and output counts
first, and fail before reading the inputs or outputs if more of them
are claimed than can fit in a block, given their minimum size (41 bytes
for an input, 9 for an output). Such a transaction can never be valid.

This allows us to allocate the vin and vout vectors immediately, rather
than sequentially in batches of 5 MB as the std::vector deserializer
does, because that memory becomes bounded: to 2.7 MB for 24390 inputs,
and 5.3 MB for 111111 outputs. It is a preparation for further changes
that rely on this structuring of conditionals.

This affects all places where transactions are deserialized. Through
RPC, such transactions can no longer be decoded. From P2P, a transaction
or block containing one is ignored like other malformed messages, rather
than rejected by validation.

p2p: reject transactions without inputs or outputs when deserializing

Add a reject_empty flag to TransactionSerParams, which makes
deserialization fail as soon as a transaction is found to have no
inputs or no outputs. Such transactions are never valid, but are
currently fully deserialized (along with the rest of the message) before
validation rejects them.

This reduces the memory a peer can make us allocate by sending a block
full of such transactions. At 10 bytes each, about 400000 of them fit in
a block message, each of which gets its own CTransaction. With this
change, the smallest transaction that gets deserialized has one input
and one output, which takes 60 bytes.

The flag is enabled (as TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P) only where transactions are
received from P2P peers: tx and block messages, and the transactions in
cmpctblock and blocktxn messages. Like other malformed messages, these
are now ignored, rather than, for a block, causing the peer to be
disconnected, or, for a transaction, being added to the reject filters.
The functional tests are updated accordingly.

refactor: use the stream's parameters for compact block transactions

BlockTransactions and PrefilledTransaction (de)serialized their
transactions with TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P, overriding any parameters of the
stream. Use the stream's parameters instead, like CBlock does, and pass
TX_WITH_WITNESS where they are serialized and TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P where
data from peers is deserialized. This does not change behavior
(serialization only depends on allow_witness), but makes it possible to
deserialize them with other parameters. Tests that are not about data
from peers do so, with TX_WITH_WITNESS.

serialize: add StreamHasParams concept Constrain ParamsStream::GetParams

() to the parameter types that the stream, or a stream it wraps, has. Before, calling it for another type failed inside the function body, which cannot be tested for. With that, add a StreamHasParams concept, which tells whether GetParams

() can be called on a stream of type Stream. This does not change what compiles. Calling GetParams

() for a type the stream does not have is now reported as an unsatisfied constraint at the call site.

serialize: add support for mutable state when (de)serializing with params

Let serialization parameters come with state: if a params type has a
State type and an InitState() method, a ParamsStream with such params
holds a State, initialized with InitState(). (De)serialization code can
read and modify it through GetState<Params>(), like it reads the params
through GetParams<Params>(). Whether a stream holds the state of a
params type can be checked with the StreamHasState concept.

This makes it possible to keep track of something across everything
that is (de)serialized through one stream, for example to limit the
total size of what is deserialized, while the params themselves stay
immutable.

As a copy of a ParamsStream would have a state of its own, make it
non-copyable.

Giving params to a stream that already has params of that type would
hide the state which the stream holds for them behind a new one. Let
params types forbid this by having a NO_OVERRIDE member, which makes
doing so a compile-time error.

Co-authored-by: Pieter Wuille <bitcoin-dev@wuille.net>

p2p: limit the weight of transactions and blocks while deserializing

Add an optional weight limit to TransactionSerParams. When it is set,
the stream's state for these params holds the weight that may still be
deserialized. It is decremented while transactions are being
deserialized (charging the minimum weight of inputs and outputs before
allocating memory for them), causing failure as soon as it is exceeded.
The limit thus applies to all transactions that are deserialized
through one stream together, such as those of a block.

As giving TransactionSerParams to a stream that already has them would
start a new state, with a limit of its own, for what is deserialized
with them, mark them as NO_OVERRIDE. For the same reason, do not allow
the deserializing constructor that takes params to be used with such a
stream.

Set the limit to MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT minus the header in
TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P, which is what tx, block, cmpctblock and blocktxn
messages are deserialized with: the transactions in a block, cmpctblock
or blocktxn message are part of one block (for blocktxn, this does not
account for those of the block that are already known), and a
transaction that does not fit in a block cannot be valid.

The P2P message size limit allows blocks of up to 4 MB, which is up to
16M weight, all of which is currently deserialized before validation
rejects it (unless a transaction has more inputs or outputs than fit in
a block). With this change, the weight deserialized from a message is
at most MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT minus the header.

Messages exceeding the limit are ignored, like other malformed
messages, rather than causing the peer to be disconnected for sending an
invalid block.

Co-authored-by: Anthony Towns <aj@erisian.com.au>

comments.body:
nit in the first commit: I mostly only wrote this test for fun in b55555da3e25a47f1e7fced7f09d4f0bf8198624. There is no need to retain the code exactly. It would also be fine to just use:

```py
        self.log.info('A really large transaction')
        tx = tx_from_hex(raw_tx_reference)
        assert_equal(len(tx.vin[0].serialize()), 41)
        tx.vin = [tx.vin[0]] * (MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT // (WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR * 41))
        self.check_mempool_result(
            result_expected=[{'txid': tx.txid_hex, 'allowed': False, 'reject-reason': 'bad-txns-oversize'}],
            rawtxs=[tx.serialize().hex()],
        )
```

to keep it brief and in symmetry with the below check.

comments.body:
My concern is/was mostly with something like a change `READWRITE(block.vtx);` into `READWRITE(TX_WITH_WITNESS(block.vtx));`, which would introduce a new scope without limiting, or a scope with limiting but a different variable (this exact example might not work, but you see what I mean).

I've switched to your approach, but added a feature for parameters to declare they cannot be overridden, which would satisfy that concern and doesn't cause any compilation problems.
